items.title: For Russia and Ukraine, an Escalating Spiral With No End in Sight
items.summary: Each side is using missiles and drones to try to pound the other into giving up, breeding ceaseless human suffering. But there is no sign that either country’s determination will weaken.

items.title: Norway Seizes Russian Ship, Testing Moscow in the High Arctic
items.summary: Empowered by an international court order, Norway captured the vessel as part of a global effort to seize Russian assets. The Russians called it “piracy.”

items.title: How Do You Run for Office in a Gang War?
items.summary: Haitian election officials have set elections for Dec. 13, but many experts say extreme violence is likely to cause a postponement. Again.

items.title: Spain’s Leader Questions Morocco Border Control During Ceuta Migrant Surge
items.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez of Spain said the role of Moroccan authorities at key moments needed to be “clarified.” But he rejected any suggestion they had planned the crisis.

items.title: Syrians Want Justice for Assad-Era Killings and Torture
items.summary: Hundreds of thousands were killed and tortured. But prosecuting everyone involved in atrocities could be impractical and risk renewed civil strife.

items.title: Israeli Military Kills Two Palestinian Youths in Village Raid, Residents Say
items.summary: Al Mughayir, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, has become a focal point for rising settler violence, with the latest deadly episode starting in a dispute over livestock.

items.title: Rival Ukrainian Intelligence Units Open Fire Against Each Other in Kyiv
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky described the shootout on the streets of the Ukrainian capital as an “absolutely shameful event” and ordered an investigation.

items.title: Israel Is Expected to Release Lebanese Prisoners, in Rare Sign of Progress
items.summary: The move would come amid struggling talks between Israel and Lebanon aimed at disarming Hezbollah and ending Israel’s invasion.

items.title: China Boycotts a Top Art Festival Over Taiwan Exhibition
items.summary: China said the Gwangju Biennale in South Korea was misrepresenting Taiwan as an independent nation. Beijing claims it as its own.

items.title: Many Italians Long Resisted Air-Conditioning. Then Europe Got Hotter.
items.summary: Amid record-breaking temperatures on the continent, households and businesses in Italy are increasingly installing cooling units.

items.title: Former Labor Secretary Stoked Dysfunction and Toxicity, Department Report Finds
items.summary: Lori Chavez-DeRemer spent Labor Department funds on personal travel and tolerated harassment in the agency, its inspector general found.

items.title: F.C.C. Asks Court to Toss ABC Suit Over Broadcast Licenses
items.summary: The network sued the agency last month to stop it from taking steps that could force ABC stations off the air. The F.C.C. said the lawsuit was premature.

items.title: Tesla Begins Offering Rides in a Car Without a Steering Wheel
items.summary: The new Cybercab embodies Elon Musk’s vision of cars that drive themselves, but it is not clear when the vehicle will be widely available.

items.title: Volkswagen Plans to Cut 50,000 Jobs
items.summary: Facing growing competition from China and rapidly advancing technology, the German auto giant said its board had approved a “comprehensive” overhaul.

items.title: Mortgage Rates Hit 6.71%, Their Highest Level Since July 2025
items.summary: Higher costs for home loans have put a squeeze on the housing market, adding pressure to consumers already struggling with elevated inflation.

items.title: Maria Bartiromo Is Out at Fox News
items.summary: The host, who appeared on Fox Business and Fox News, had been with the network for more than 12 years.

items.title: Bessent Blames Ukraine for High Energy Prices
items.summary: After meeting with Russia’s finance minister, the Treasury secretary said Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure were contributing to a global energy shock driven mainly by the U.S. war with Iran.

items.title: Leon Black Sues Congressional Panel Investigating Epstein
items.summary: The billionaire skipped a deposition on Thursday and filed a lawsuit seeking to block a House committee’s subpoenas demanding nondisclosure agreements he may have made with women.

items.title: The Athletic Says Dianna Russini’s Relationship With Mike Vrabel Violated Its Standards
items.summary: The New York Times-owned publication said the relationship between its former reporter Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel of the Patriots gave the appearance of a conflict of interest.

items.title: Schools Giving Aid to Minority Students Could Lose Tax Exemptions Under Trump’s New Rules
items.summary: The Treasury Department released rules that would prevent schools with race-based programs from qualifying for tax-exempt status, a threat to both higher education and other private schools.

items.title: Nvidia Buys Hugging Face in $12.9 Billion Deal
items.summary: The acquisition of the start-up is an indication of Nvidia’s growing role as Silicon Valley’s central banker and its emphasis on open-source technology.

items.title: Which Investors Will Get Rich From Anthropic’s IPO?
items.summary: When Anthropic goes public in a blockbuster offering, which investors will profit? The answer says a lot about how much start-up investing has changed over the years.

items.title: Why the Courts Are Hesitant to Punish Tech Giants Like Meta and Google
items.summary: After finding antitrust violations, federal courts have been reluctant to impose harsh sanctions. They fear meddling in markets where technology is racing ahead.

items.title: In a Big Win, Google Won’t Have to Break Up Its Ad Tech Business, Court Rules
items.summary: In a long-awaited decision, a federal judge said Google must change its ad tech business to address antitrust issues, but did not disclose the measures.

items.title: Why the Hugging Face Hack Should Make You Worry More About A.I.
items.summary: The attack by an aggressive “collective” of OpenAI agents shows the danger of artificial intelligence systems that organize themselves.

items.title: How OpenAI Limited the Probe of Its Bots’ Hack of Hugging Face
items.summary: A nonprofit’s study of how OpenAI’s A.I. agents were able to break into Hugging Face’s infrastructure wasn’t allowed to look at the incident’s full scope.

items.title: Noise and Motion Monitors in Their Homes? These Tenants Say No.
items.summary: The public housing authority in Concord, N.H., installed monitoring devices in 300 homes. Tenants are now suing to remove the Minut sensors.

items.title: Justice Dept. Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Suit
items.summary: The department argued in a court filing that OpenAI legally used articles by The New York Times to develop A.I., adding that national security depended on American tech dominance.

items.title: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
items.summary: He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.

items.title: Uber Lays Off 10% of Employees in Sweeping Reorganization
items.summary: The layoffs affect about 3,300 workers, as Chief Executive Dara Khosrowshahi bets on a “leaner organization.”
